_about: The small motions the original's scripts give an entity: linearMotion, and the callbacks that
call it. Decoded from android_game.bin through the remake's asbc listing
step 3.2 (the remake's out/parity/visuals/briefs/00_order.md section 7; systems_9_10.md 10b), planning
Every number below is the script's. The one thing that is not is the start angle each crystal or
key is given: the original draws it with randF(PI) from a generator re-seeded from its clock, so
its phases are unrecoverable and the port draws its own, from a stream in the level's drawing order
seeded for each level with MagicPortalsLayer's kMotionSeed mixed with the level's name
(Motion::LevelSeed). Only their distribution is the original's.
A motion moves the PICTURE and what the entity carries (its sparkles, a timed crystal's dial). The
port keeps pick-up on the node: the original tests its 26 u range from the moved position, at most
1.5 u away, and the port's crystal and key tests do not move (a recorded divergence, systems_9_10

_source: linearMotion(ETHEntity thisEntity, bool vertical, float angle, float startAngle),
utilEntityEffect.angelscript bytes 327527..328407:
ins 1-12    CheckCustomData('originalPos'); when absent (the first call):
ins 13-27   SetVector3('originalPos', GetPosition())
ins 28-39   SetFloat('angle', startAngle)
ins 41-51   speed = GetFloat('speed')
ins 53-68   AddToFloat('angle', g_timeManager.unitsPerSecond(speed))
ins 70-98   if GetFloat('angle') > PI x 2f (CpyGtoV4 PI; MULIf 2f; CMPf; JNP):
AddToFloat('angle', -PI x 2f). Once, not a modulo
ins 100-110 stride = GetFloat('stride')
ins 112-129 offset = cos(GetFloat('angle')) x stride x sign(speed)
ins 131-142 m = rotateZ(degreeToRadian(angle))
ins 144-178 v = vertical ? vector3(0, offset, 0) : vector3(offset, 0, 0); v = multiply(v, m)
ins 180-208 SetPosition(GetVector3('originalPos') + v x g_scale.getScale())
So the angle is stepped BEFORE the offset is read, and the first frame drawn already has one step
in it (00_order 8.0 rule 6: the draw reads the position the callback wrote).
STimeManager::unitsPerSecond(float speed), STimeManager.angelscript bytes 8045..8162: ins 3-15
speed x min(200, GetLastFrameElapsedTime()) / 1000.0 (SetV8 shows the low bits only; the constant is
exactly 1000.0, 00_order 8.0 rule 2); ins 16-18 x m_factor, which STimeManager's constructor sets to
1 and pause() to 0. frame_cap_ms is that 200.
wrap_rad is PI x 2f in float: PI is registered as the float 3.141592654f
(ETHScriptObjRegister.cpp:512-515, GameMath.h's constant::PI), so 6.2831854820251465.
rotateZ and multiply: Ethanon GameMath.h RotateZ builds rows (cos, sin; -sin, cos) and
Multiply(Vector3, Matrix4x4) takes (x a11 + y a12, x a21 + y a22), bound as multiply(const vector3 &in,
const matrix4x4 &in) (ETHScriptWrapper.Math.generic.cpp:55): (x cos a + y sin a, -x sin a + y cos a),
a positive angle turning counter-clockwise on the +y-down screen.
g_scale.getScale() is m_scaleFactor, screen height / 256 (00_order 8.12a): the level's units times it
are screen pixels, so in the port's level units it is 1 and the amplitude is the stride.
ETHCallback_crystal, ETHCallback_crystal.angelscript bytes 424324..424766, every frame the crystal
lives (entity names crystal and crystal.ent: 35 and 435 placements, both run ETHCallback_crystal):
ins 1-12    CheckCustomData('speed') != 0 skips to ins 83. No crystal placement carries `speed`
(systems_9_10's census10: 470 crystals, 0 with speed), so every one takes the defaults:
ins 14-25   SetFloat('speed', 2f)
ins 27-38   SetFloat('stride', 1.5f)
ins 40-58   squaredRange = scale(26)^2 (the pick-up range; the port's Goals keeps its own test)
ins 60-82   a uint `time`: addTimerToCrystal (step 68's dial) and the temp-alert sound
ins 83-96   linearMotion(thisEntity, vertical = true (SetV1 1), angle = 0f, startAngle =
randF(PI)). A call pushes its last argument first (00_order 8.0 rule 3): the randF
result at ins 87 is startAngle, the 0f at ins 88 is angle, the 1 at ins 89-90 vertical
randF(PI) is Randomizer::Float(PI), m_mt.rand(PI), uniform on [0, PI]
(ETHScriptWrapper.generic.cpp:338; gs2d Randomizer.cpp:44-47). It is called every frame and read
only on the first. So: a period of PI seconds, an amplitude of 1.5 units, a phase of its own.
crystal.ent is static=1: its callback runs only while its bucket is on screen (00_order 8.12c), so the
original starts a crystal's bob when it is first seen and holds it while it is not. The port starts
every crystal on the level's first tick; with a random phase the two cannot be told apart.
_measured: systems_9_10 10b (bob2.py, bob_period.py) on the original's library frames: 161 crystals in 74
levels; peak-to-peak over a crystal's frames median 1.60 u, p90 2.85, max 3.38 (the decode's
period fit's nearest minimum 3.20 s. Phases differ per crystal (same-frame spread median 1.60 u).

_source: ETHCallback_key, ETHCallback_key.angelscript bytes 438490..442683 (entity names key and key.ent: 8
and 31 placements; key_pos is another entity):
ins 1-12    CheckCustomData('speed') != 0 skips the setup; no key carries `speed`
ins 14-38   SetFloat('speed', 2f); SetFloat('stride', 1.5f)
ins 60-71   SetInt('ownerID', -1)
ins 204-220 GetUInt('foundKeyhole') != 0: the fly-in to its keyhole (ins 221-652), which never
reaches the bob
ins 653-665 GetInt('ownerID') >= 0 (CMPIi 0; JNS): the carried branch at ins 860
ins 666-679 otherwise linearMotion(thisEntity, true, 0f, randF(PI)), the crystal's call, and
then the pick-up scan from the moved position (ins 680-857)
ins 978-991 the carried branch writes SetVector3('originalPos', GetPosition()) every frame and
never touches `angle`
So a key bobs only while no one carries it and it has not found its keyhole; a dropped key bobs
about where it was dropped and takes up its swing at the angle it was picked up at. key.ent is
static=0, so its callback runs on every frame, seen or not.
ETHCallback_hand_drawn_arrow, MiscCallbacks.angelscript bytes 343339..343470, every frame (entity
hand_drawn_arrow.ent, static=1: 8 placements, on 1-01, 1-08, 1-09, 1-10 at 45, 1-12 at 50 and -50, and
2-32 twice):
ins 1       PshC4 0f                   startAngle = 0 (a call pushes its last argument first)
ins 2-5     GetAngle()                 angle = the entity's own angle
ins 6-7     SetV1 v3, v0; PshV4        vertical = 0, false (00_order 8.0 rule 1: v0 is the constant 0)
ins 8-13    linearMotion(thisEntity, false, GetAngle(), 0f)
ins 15-17   SetAlpha(0.55f)
So it swings along its own angle by its node's stride at its node's speed (every placement carries
speed 4 and stride 2.5: a period of pi/2 s, 2.5 units either way), starting a whole stride forward, at
alpha 0.55 over the colour the level gave it (SetAlpha writes m_v4Color.w, ETHEntity.cpp:505-508).

_source: ETHCallback_dashed_circle, MiscCallbacks.angelscript bytes 342895..343043, every frame (entity
dashed_circle.ent, static=1: 9 placements, on 1-02, 1-03 twice, 1-05 twice, 1-16 twice and 4-05 twice):
ins 1       PshC4 0f                   startAngle = 0
ins 2       PshC4 0f                   angle = 0, a constant: the turn below never tilts the bob
ins 3-4     SetV1 v3, v1; PshV4        vertical = 1, true
ins 5-10    linearMotion(thisEntity, true, 0f, 0f)
ins 12-14   SetAlpha(0.55f)
ins 16-23   AddToAngle(g_timeManager.unitsPerSecond(8f)): 8 degrees a second, capped and paused as
linear_motion's step is. AddToAngle adds to m_angle (ETHEntityController.cpp:145-148),
which the draw turns the picture by, counter-clockwise on the screen
(ETHRenderEntity.cpp:105, GLES2Sprite.cpp:268-270; the converter wrote it negated, tscn.py:432-433).
So it bobs up and down by its node's stride at its node's speed (every placement: 0.6 units, 1.5 rad/s,
a period of 4.19 s), from 0.6 below, turning 8 degrees a second, at alpha 0.55.
ETHCallback_dashed_square, MiscCallbacks.angelscript bytes 343043..343129, every frame (entity
dashed_square.ent, static=1: 1 placement, on 1-08):
ins 1-3     SetAlpha(0.55f), and nothing else.
Its .ent and its node carry speed 1.5 and stride 0.6, which no call reads: it does not move.
ETHCallback_hand_tap, MiscCallbacks.angelscript bytes 344140..344990, every frame (entity hand_tap.ent,
static=0: 7 placements, on 1-02, 1-03 twice, 1-16 twice (one at 95 degrees) and 1-27 twice):
ins 1       PshC4 0f                   startAngle = 0
ins 2-6     GetAngle(); SUBIf 90f      angle = the entity's own angle less 90
ins 7-8     SetV1 v2, v0; PshV4        vertical = 0, false
ins 9-14    linearMotion(thisEntity, false, GetAngle() - 90f, 0f)
ins 16-22   only when not paused: the touches, and ins 60-170 a release within scale(30) of it adds
smoke_vanish.ent and deletes it (System 7's, not built here)
No SetAlpha anywhere in the callback (null): it is drawn at the alpha the level gives it. A hand at angle
0 swings along 0 - 90, which rotateZ turns down the screen; every placement carries speed 3 and
stride 4 (a period of 2.09 s, 4 units either way).

_placed_notes: Every one of the 25 placements above carries both `speed` and `stride` (the port's test_mp_motion census);
Motion::FromNode refuses a node without them, and the layer then draws it still, as GetFloat's 0 would.
None of the four .ent files has a particle system and no node carries a light or a halo, so nothing but the
picture moves; and no row draws a random start angle, so the crystals' and keys' start-angle stream draws
